title: Northwind — Securing a PaaS web application
scenario: Northwind is deploying a web app (App Service) and an Azure SQL Database to Azure. The solution must not expose the database or the web app directly to the public internet, and secrets must never be stored in code.
context: The SQL database must be reachable only from within the virtual network.
The web app must authenticate to the database without hard-coded credentials.
Threat detection is required for the database.

questions.prompt: How should Northwind make the SQL database reachable only from within the VNet?
options: Use a private endpoint for the SQL database
Allow all Azure services through the SQL firewall
Assign the database a public IP
Disable the VNet
questions.explanation: A private endpoint gives the SQL database a private IP inside the VNet, removing public exposure.

questions.prompt: How should the web app authenticate to the database without hard-coded credentials?
options: Enable a system-assigned managed identity on the App Service and grant it database access
Store the password in the web.config file
Embed the connection string in the front-end HTML
Share the SQL admin password
questions.explanation: A managed identity provides Entra-based authentication to Azure resources with no stored credentials.

questions.prompt: Which two capabilities satisfy the auditing and threat-detection requirements?
options: Enable SQL auditing and Defender for Databases
Enable Azure Bastion and Network Watcher
Enable Azure Front Door and CDN
Enable Key Vault and Event Hubs only
questions.explanation: SQL auditing records database events, and Defender for Databases provides threat detection and vulnerability assessment.

title: Tailwind Traders — Identity hardening and monitoring
scenario: Tailwind Traders wants to reduce standing privileged access and improve visibility into security events. They also need automated responses to high-severity incidents.
context: Administrators should get elevated permissions only when needed and only for a limited time.
Risky or unusual sign-ins must prompt additional verification.
Centralize security logs from Azure and Microsoft 365 for analysis.
Automatically isolate a compromised VM when a high-severity alert fires.

questions.prompt: What should be used to grant administrators elevated permissions only when needed?
options: Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
Permanent Global Administrator assignment
A shared admin account
Azure Policy
questions.explanation: PIM provides just-in-time, time-bound, approval-based role activation.

questions.prompt: How should risky or unusual sign-ins be handled?
options: Create a Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for risky sign-ins
Block all users permanently
Disable MFA to reduce friction
Ignore the risk signals
questions.explanation: Conditional Access can use sign-in risk as a signal and challenge with MFA or block.

questions.prompt: What should Tailwind Traders use to centralize logs and automatically respond to incidents?
options: Microsoft Sentinel with data connectors and automation rules (playbooks)
A spreadsheet of logs
Azure Front Door only
Azure Bastion
questions.explanation: Sentinel is a SIEM/SOAR that ingests logs via connectors and automates response with playbooks.
